summary: Redwood AE and SE walked SearchNova through hosted embeddings + rerank API workflow, demoed Console search-relevance flow, and discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs. Customer is evaluating hosted first, with possible Dedicated if latency/cost needs tighten. Agreed to provide sample data for benchmark POC; Redwood to send pricing and security docs.
topics: Console demo: relevance tuning and Optimize suggestions
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lena, AE on the account, and with me is Marcus from Solutions Engineering. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Shah: Priya here, head of search at SearchNova.
[00:10] Tom Reynolds: Tom, engineering.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Aisha, data science.
[00:15] Marcus Lin: Hey team, Marcus, SE. Real quick agenda: we'll do a 20–25 minute demo of hosted embeddings and the rerank flow, show the Console relevance tuning, then leave time for Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Priya: Sounds good. we're mainly evaluating a hosted option first, right — we want low lift, but we do have some strict latency p95 targets.
[00:35] Lena: Yes exactly, we'll show both the default hosted flow and how you can optimize with batching, caching, and the Optimize suggestions for cost/perf.
[00:44] Marcus: Ok jumping in — native embeddings first. We call the embeddings endpoint, you get a vector per doc, store in your vector DB or Redwood's managed index; then at query time you do a candidate retrieval and then call the rerank endpoint which uses the model to score candidates.
[01:05] Marcus: (screen share) here's the API request pattern — embed docs with /v1/embeddings, store them. For search realtime we typically do a hybrid approach, BM25 to narrow candidates then rerank.
[01:22] Tom: Sorry, can you repeat the rerank API path? I heard something like /v1/rer —
[01:26] Marcus: It's /v1/rerank, yep. Example payloads in the SDKs — side note our SDKs handle batching and retry logic.
[01:34] Aisha: How much latency are we looking at for rerank if we send 100 candidates?
[01:39] Marcus: Good question — depends on model size and hosted config. For our verified profile with a 2B-ish rerank model, p50 is ~30–60ms per request when scoring 100 candidates with continuous batching on shared hosted. p95 can be higher, 180–300ms, but we can tune with smaller models or dedicated pool.
[02:05] Priya: Hmm that's in the ballpark. Our p95 budget is 250ms for the search path end-to-end, so we need to budget for retrieval + rerank + app logic.
[02:15] Lena: Right, and we'd run a quick perf test on your sample workload to give tighter numbers. Marcus will set up a benchmark with your queries and docs.
[02:22] Marcus: I'll also test the KV cache for popular prefixes; note sometimes the transcript generator writes K-V cash, but it's K-V cache — that can shave tokens and latency when you have repetitive queries.
[02:35] Tom: About cost — if we do heavy reranking at 100 candidates per query our token cost looks pretty high. Do you have guidance?
[02:42] Marcus: Absolutely. That's where batching, candidate pruning (BM25 top 10 then rerank) and quantized models help. Our Optimize tool in Console actually suggests quantization and batching settings per workload.
[02:55] Marcus: (switching tab) Here's the Redwood Console — per-route metrics, token breakdown, latency. You can see how embeddings and rerank calls contribute to cost.
[03:10] Priya: Is it easy to flip to a smaller model for rerank in the flow? We want to test something lighter before committing.
[03:15] Lena: Yes you can route by model variant — the API supports model param and the Console has rollout controls for canarying a cheaper model.
[03:24] Aisha: A quick question on relevance quality — do you provide any tooling to test regressions when swapping models?
[03:29] Marcus: Yep. We have eval harnesses — you can inject labeled prompts and Redwood Optimize will run regressions and alert if semantic drift increases.
[03:37] Tom: Security — we require SOC2, SAML SSO, enterprise KMS, and the data can't be used for model training.
[03:44] Lena: We have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO and customer-managed KMS options for Private/Dedicated; for hosted we provide encryption at rest and in transit and strict data use commitments — we'll attach the security pack.
[03:58] Priya: Are audit logs available for requests? We need per-request tracing for compliance.
[04:03] Marcus: Yes, per-route tracing, token-level logs, and you can export audit logs to your syslog/S3.
[04:10] Priya: Great. Any region/data residency options? We're EU-centric.
[04:14] Lena: Hosted supports region pinning; if you need strict residency we can do Dedicated or Private inside EU regions.
[04:20] Tom: Ok thanks. Back to cost: can you show a concrete example of the rerank payload and how you compute cost per rerank call?
[04:28] Marcus: (shares code) Example: rerank call takes the query + list of candidate docs (IDs + snippets); cost is per token processed by the model plus model selection. We show token breakdown in Console. For 100 short snippets it's more tokens, for top-10 it's much cheaper.
[04:48] Aisha: We typically generate around 50–120 tokens per snippet in our current pipeline — that could add up.
[04:52] Marcus: Then I'd recommend aggressive candidate pruning upstream, or provide richer embeddings that get higher precision retrieval.
[05:00] Lena: Quick live demo — Marcus will run a sample query against a demo index we preloaded; you'll see candidate generation + rerank scoring in Console.
[05:07] Marcus: (typing) running query now... [05:12] results populated — list of candidates then rerank scores, you can inspect gradients or scoring features.
[05:20] Priya: Looks clean. I see a couple items where the rerank bumped less relevant results — is there a way to tune feature weights?
[05:27] Marcus: Console has a relevance tuning pane — you can create a small training set, define labels, and run a tuning job. Optimize then suggests model/config changes.
[05:36] Tom: If we want to try dedicated capacity for steady low-latency, what's the procurement lead time?
[05:41] Lena: Dedicated typically requires a minimum 3-month commit and provisioning can be a week or two depending on region and GPUs. Enterprise legal + contract adds time.
[05:51] Priya: That's fine, we may pilot hosted first then move to Dedicated if perf/cost needs require it.
[05:57] Aisha: One more technical — how does Redwood handle KV cache eviction across requests? For long session contexts we worry about memory.
[06:06] Marcus: The runtime manages KV cache with LRU-ish eviction tuned per model and seq length. If you're doing large contexts we can recommend model variants or chunking.
[06:16] Tom: Any gotchas with our current stack? We're on Kubernetes, use Elastic for indexing, and host in GCP europe-west1.
[06:25] Marcus: No major gotchas — we integrate with Elastic. For routing you can route from your infra to hosted region or use our managed index connectors; we can share an architecture doc.
[06:34] Priya: Can you also show how the SDK handles retries and backoff? We saw some jitter in spikes during internal tests.
[06:39] Marcus: Sure — SDK has built-in exponential backoff and idempotency keys for certain calls; for heavy real-time traffic we recommend a local circuit-breaker layer.
[06:48] Lena: Quick pause — any other compliance questions?
[06:51] Tom: Data retention policy — we need 90-day retention and ability to purge on demand.
[06:55] Lena: We support configurable retention and on-demand data deletes; Redwood not trained on customer data per contract. We'll attach the DPA and data handling details.
[07:03] Priya: Great. Back to the demo — can the rerank endpoint accept rich features besides raw text?
[07:09] Marcus: Yes you can pass structured features per candidate, like recency, CTR signals, etc. The rerank model can incorporate those as additional inputs.
[07:19] Aisha: For your eval harness, are there CLI tools or is it via Console?
[07:23] Marcus: Both — CLI for automation, Console for quick experiments.
[07:28] Lena: Ok wrapping toward next steps: we'll run a benchmark on your dataset, send pricing and security docs, and schedule follow-up POC kickoff.
[07:37] Priya: Good. How long will the benchmark take?
[07:40] Marcus: For a 10k query set, end-to-end profiling is about 1–2 hours to get reliable p95 numbers.
[07:46] Tom: Perfect.
[07:48] Lena: Any final questions?
[07:50] Priya: Not from me. I'll loop in infra and legal once we have pricing and security docs.
[07:56] Tom: We'll provide the dataset by Friday.
[07:59] Lena: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the items noted.
[08:03] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels — speaker labels auto-generated; some technical terms transcribed as "K-V cash" or "Sam-el". The team agreed on concrete next steps: sample dataset + benchmark + pricing/security packet.
